answer: An agent market can allocate buying votes in proportion to locked collateral, with each unit of collateral counted only once across all identities. Whether agents predict a zephyr at dawn or trade power as the tide turns, creating extra accounts adds no voting weight: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. An attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital to gain control, sacrificing liquidity and other returns.
